cues.text: Now the man-made fabrics. Many of these do not like high heat.
Polyester is made from plastic. It is strong and does not wrinkle much. Too much heat can make it shiny or even melt it.
Nylon is strong and light. You find it in jackets and linings. Use low heat.
Rayon, also called viscose, is made from wood pulp. It is soft and flowy, but very weak when wet, and it can shrink. Dry clean it.
Acetate is shiny and is used for linings and dresses. Use low heat. Perfume and nail polish remover can melt it.
Spandex makes clothes stretch. It is also called elastane or Lycra. Heat can ruin the stretch.
Most clothes are a mix of fabrics, like sixty percent cotton and forty percent polyester.
Always treat a mix like the most delicate fabric in it.
Leather, suede, fur, and wedding gowns need special care. Always ask a manager before you take them in.
